Response custom rules

WAF

The response firewall can block responses before they reach visitors. Cloudflare turns on default protections for everyone, on every plan.

Every plan includes three response custom rules per zone. These rules run in the http_response_firewall_custom phase.

Rules support the block, log, and execute actions. You can include at most one execute rule within the three-rule allowance.

Oct 20, 2026

Think agents now use a @cloudflare/computer workspace

AgentsWorkers

Think and Agent Skills now use the workspace from @cloudflare/computer ↗︎ as well as the filesystem tools. A JavaScript execution environment can be configured by adding the WorkerJavaScriptBackend.

@cloudflare/shell is deprecated, and so is Think's createExecuteTool. These will no longer be developed nor supported from today onwards.

Migrate your workspace data

This is a breaking change. @cloudflare/computer stores files in different tables from @cloudflare/shell, and there is no automatic data migration between workspace formats. To keep an existing workspace, copy its files with the script in Migrating from @cloudflare/shell to @cloudflare/computer ↗︎. Otherwise your agent will start with an empty workspace, though the original data will still be present in the existing tables.

For more information, refer to Think tools.

Oct 20, 2026

Wrangler and cf now upload source maps by default

WorkersCloudflare CLI

From Wrangler 4.150.0, wrangler deploy, wrangler versions upload, and wrangler preview generate and upload source maps by default. You no longer need to set upload_source_maps to get stack traces with your original file names and line numbers.

cf deploy also uploads source maps by default. With the Cloudflare Vite plugin 1.64.0 or later, Worker builds generate source maps by default, and cf deploy uploads every source map in the build output.

Remapped stack traces show up in Workers Logs, real-time logs, Tail Workers, and Workers Issues. Source maps are applied after your Worker runs, so they don't affect CPU time, bundle size, or cold starts.

If your Worker uses a custom build, Wrangler uploads any external source maps it finds. Maps it can't resolve, such as inline data: source maps, are skipped instead of failing the upload. Set upload_source_maps to true if you'd prefer the upload to fail.

To opt out with Wrangler, set upload_source_maps to false:

To opt out with cf or the Cloudflare Vite plugin, set build.sourcemap to false for your Worker's Vite environment. Refer to Disable source maps.

Oct 19, 2026

Cloudflare API MCP server now supports step-up authorization

Agents

The Cloudflare API MCP server now supports step-up authorization ↗︎.

Grant only the required scopes when you connect, then authorize more on demand as your agent performs a task. When a tool call needs a scope you have not granted, the server returns an insufficient_scope challenge ↗︎ naming it, and your MCP client asks you to approve it. Scopes you already granted are kept.

To start with the least access, choose Minimal on the consent page when you connect https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp. Refer to authorization in MCP.

Available now in all MCP clients that support step-up authorization.

Oct 19, 2026

Precursor adds Monitor mode

Bots

We released Monitor mode at customers' request so they can test Precursor and the Precursor Interstitial without updating bot score.

In Security > Settings, the Precursor Status dropdown now offers Off, Monitor, and Arm. Selecting Arm means Precursor detections can affect bot score and Challenge clearance. Selecting Monitor means Precursor detections do not affect bot score or Challenge clearance.

We also separated the Precursor Interstitial from the mode. Set the sitewide default with Show Interstitial, then add Interstitial Rules to customize it for specific requests. For example, leave Show Interstitial off across most of your site, but require an interstitial Challenge on /checkout to enforce a valid session before purchase.

For more information, refer to the Precursor documentation.

Oct 19, 2026

Cloud Workload Security is now available in Beta

Cloud Workload Security

Cloud Workload Security (CWS) is now available in Beta. Apply policy controls to cloud API requests before they reach your cloud provider.

Define policies with request filters and Rego checks. For example, block requests that would make an R2 bucket public. Use workloads and policy sets to target your cloud environments.

Manage your policies in the Cloudflare dashboard. Run the CWS proxy in your environment and route client requests through it to enforce your policies.

CWS requires a Zero Trust subscription. The Zero Trust Free plan is sufficient.

To configure your first guardrail, follow Get started with Cloud Workload Security.

Oct 19, 2026

Introducing Clairic: an extraction model for typed values, now on Workers AI

Workers AI

@cf/cloudflare/clairic is now available on Workers AI as a preview. Clairic is the first extraction model: a System One model that answers with values instead of text. We intend to release the model with open weights soon.

Decision models such as Clef choose among options you define up front. Many structured-output tasks do not have answers you can list in advance: an invoice total, a delivery date, the number of days a shipment is late, or what a repair will cost. Clairic handles these. You send a state and a schema of typed fields, and it returns one typed value per field. A value is read from the input, computed from it, or predicted beyond it.

Clairic does not generate tokens. It reads your input in one pass and decodes each answer under the rules of its type, so every answer is a valid value of the type you asked for, or null when the input does not determine it.

Typed fields

Define as many fields as you need. Fields that do not fit beside the input in one pass are split across parallel passes, so there is no upper limit.

Type Returns
text An exact span of the input, with its character offsets
number A number read or worked out from the input, honoring integer and decimals
date, time, datetime Real calendar dates and valid times, in ISO form
duration A length of time in the unit you choose
list Every matching text, number, or date, in input order
estimate A distribution inside your min and max, on your step grid, on a linear or log scale
forecast One estimate per future step of a series, up to 64 steps

Every scalar answer includes p_null, the probability that the input does not determine the value, and a confidence score. Estimates and forecasts include a median and an 80% interval (p10 to p90). Set options.include_quantiles to also get all 99 percentiles. Use these to decide what to automate and what to send to review.

You can also pass up to four images alongside the state.

Preview

The current endpoint is an early checkpoint, and we expect it to improve:

  • Arithmetic: One- and two-step calculations, such as totals, differences, conversions, and date arithmetic, are reliable. Long chains of dependent steps and aggregations across many table rows are not yet. Extract the inputs with Clairic and do the math in code.
  • Estimates: Clairic estimates best when the input contains evidence such as comparables, history, or descriptive text. Without evidence, the interval is wide.
  • Forecasts: Forecasting is basic. Next-step forecasts follow recent patterns, but forecasts several steps out flatten toward the average, and Clairic does not anticipate events the series does not show, such as holidays. It does not replace a time-series model trained on your data.
  • Calibration: Intervals are trained to be calibrated and are on most held-out sets, but they can run narrow on unfamiliar data.
  • Confidence: Every answer is well formed, not necessarily correct. Use confidence, p_null, and the intervals to decide what to automate and what to send to review.
  • Dates: Dates without a year are resolved from context. If a field depends on the current date, set reference_date or add a line such as Today: 2026-10-19 to the state.

Pricing

Clairic costs $0.10 per million input tokens. Because it generates no tokens, there is no output token charge.

Get started

Use Clairic through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()) or the REST API at /ai/run. You can also use AI Gateway with these endpoints.

For more information, refer to the Clairic model page, extraction models, pricing, and the blog post ↗︎.

Oct 19, 2026

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 now available on Workers AI

Workers AI

@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 is now available on Workers AI. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 552B backbone parameters. It activates 8B parameters per token during prefill and 16B during decode, which keeps input-heavy agentic workloads fast and low-cost.

The 1017 release is an update to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks, and it completes tasks with shorter outputs.

Key capabilities:

  • Vision: Send images alongside text in the same request.
  • Reasoning: Reasoning is on by default at high effort. Set reasoning_effort to low or max to change the effort, or to none to turn reasoning off.
  • Function calling: Build agents that invoke tools and APIs across multiple conversation turns.
  • Long context: A full 1,048,576 token context window.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash requires the Workers Paid plan or prepaid AI Gateway credits. The default rate limit is 20 requests per minute with standard Workers AI billing and 50 requests per minute with prepaid AI Gateway credits. For details, refer to limits.

Use DeepSeek V4.1 Flash through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()), the REST API, the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or AI Gateway.

For more information, refer to the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model page and pricing.

Test Cron Triggers with Local Explorer

WorkersCloudflare CLI

Local Explorer can now send one-off Cron Trigger invocations to a Worker's scheduled() handler during local development. This removes the need to construct request URLs when testing handler behavior.

Start your local development server with cf dev, wrangler dev, or the Cloudflare Vite plugin. Open /cdn-cgi/local/explorer on the server URL and select Cron Triggers.

The browser interface supports the following tasks:

  • Invoke configured cron expressions
  • Build ad hoc expressions
  • Set reusable scheduled times
  • Inspect outcomes and noRetry() status

Ad hoc triggers and scheduled time presets stay in your browser. They do not change cloudflare.config.ts, your Wrangler configuration, or deployed Cron Triggers. Local development does not run cron schedules automatically.

Full logs and traces are available in the development session that owns the Worker when that session has Observability turned on.

The following example uses port 8787. Replace it with your development server port, such as 5173 for Vite.

The Local Explorer API exposes the same operation for tools and AI agents. The request targets an exact Worker name and accepts a cron expression and optional scheduled time:

For more details, refer to Test Cron Triggers with Local Explorer.

Oct 16, 2026

AI Search keyword search supports Japanese, Chinese, and Korean queries

AI Search

AI Search keyword search with the trigram tokenizer now matches Japanese, Chinese, and Korean queries, including full natural-language questions such as 経費精算の締め日はいつですか？. Previously, a query without spaces was treated as a single exact phrase and usually returned no keyword results.

The porter tokenizer does not work well for these languages. If your content is in Japanese, Chinese, or Korean, set keyword_tokenizer to trigram. Changing the tokenizer triggers a full reindex.

Refer to Keyword search for tokenizer details.

Search Cloudflare documentation with the Cloudflare CLI

WorkersCloudflare CLI

Cloudflare CLI 1.0.0-beta.16 includes cf docs search, so you and your coding agent can find Cloudflare documentation without leaving the terminal. Search for guides, tutorials, and examples across Cloudflare products.

To install or update to the latest release:

npm install --global cf@latest
yarn global add cf@latest
pnpm add --global cf@latest
bun add --global cf@latest

Describe what you want to do, or ask a question:

The command searches live Cloudflare documentation and returns up to five ranked JSON results. Each result includes a title, description, and documentation URL. An Internet connection is required.

Agents can parse the results and fetch a complete page as Markdown. For example, use jq to select the first result, then request its URL with the Accept: text/markdown header:

This release also standardizes generated command names to kebab-case. For example, cf accounts billing getCredits becomes cf accounts billing get-credits. For the full list of breaking command and flag changes, refer to the Cloudflare CLI release notes ↗︎.

For more information, refer to Find Cloudflare documentation with a coding agent.

Oct 16, 2026

50,000 routes per account and Tunnels for Platforms

Cloudflare TunnelCloudflare Tunnel for SASECloudflare MeshCloudflare One

Two changes make it easier to run Cloudflare Tunnel at scale.

50,000 routes per account by default

The default limit for routes is now 50,000 per account, up from 1,000. This limit covers CIDR routes and hostname routes for Cloudflare Tunnel and Cloudflare Mesh. The new limit applies to every account automatically, with no action required.

Published applications (public hostnames) are not routes and are not affected by this limit. Each tunnel supports roughly 5,000–10,000 published applications, depending on the size of its configuration. For details, refer to Published application limits.

Tunnels for Platforms

Every account includes 1,000 tunnels. With Tunnels for Platforms, you can now run more than 1,000 tunnels in a single account — for example, one tunnel per device, per end customer, or per development environment.

To buy additional tunnels, go to Networking > Tunnels and select Buy more tunnels in the Usage card. Additional tunnels are billed at $4.50 per tunnel per month. Enterprise customers can contact their account team for committed or usage-based pricing.

Go to Tunnels ↗

For pricing, limits, and best practices for managing large tunnel fleets, refer to Tunnels for Platforms.

BGP route filtering for IPsec and GRE tunnels

Cloudflare WANMagic TransitCloudflare One

Cloudflare WAN and Magic Transit IPsec and GRE tunnels now support BGP import and export filtering.

Create reusable filter profiles that specify an allow or deny action and a list of Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) targets with exact, more-specific, or prefix-length matching. Each tunnel supports one import filter and one export filter.

You can create and assign profiles through the dashboard, API, or Terraform. Profile changes apply without resetting the BGP session.

Oct 15, 2026

Gateway and Workers integration is now in public beta

Cloudflare OneWorkersGateway

Cloudflare Gateway now integrates with Cloudflare Workers in public beta on all Zero Trust plans. You can use the Forward action in Gateway HTTP policies to run your own code on matching, permitted traffic without managing a separate proxy.

The Forward action lets you transform HTTP requests and responses, return a coaching page, or run background tasks such as Slack notifications and R2 captures. Your Worker receives the request and Gateway context, including connection metadata, user identity, and device posture when available.

Gateway handles the proxy connection, TLS decryption, and upstream routing. It evaluates HTTP request policies before Forward policies and inspects the final response before returning it to the user.

Gateway inspects the original request body before delivering it to your Worker. A body-inspection Block decision can interrupt the Worker.

To get started, deploy a Worker and configure a Forward policy, or adapt one of the Worker templates.

Oct 15, 2026

Ultra-low latency live with WebRTC is now Generally Available in Stream

Stream

Stream WebRTC support lets you deliver high quality live video to thousands of concurrent viewers in milliseconds. WebRTC is compatible with native Web APIs and standard protocols, so creators can go live from a browser without needing a separate broadcast application. This powers platforms to build custom experiences with deep feature integration for creators as well as viewers. Here's how to get started with a Stream live input and a browser.

Usage-based billing for WebRTC begins today, October 15, 2026 and follows the standard rates for minutes of video delivered. Refer to pricing ↗︎ for rates.

What changed

While in beta, Stream’s WebRTC support was rebuilt from the ground up to leverage Cloudflare Realtime ↗︎’s primitives for stability and scale while managing these components in Stream’s familiar, unified API that makes it easy to build. We also adopted the latest WHIP and WHEP protocol standards for Trickle ICE, server and client offer modes, and counter-offer support for improved player library compatibility and network traversal adaptability. Finally, WebRTC delivery will now be visible in Stream’s analytics ↗︎ and billable usage charts.

How does this relate to Cloudflare Realtime

Realtime exposes a set of tools and primitives to build applications that connect people, AI systems, and devices together in many-to-many experiences powered by WebRTC. Stream leverages these building-blocks to deliver one-to-many broadcast capabilities, controlled and managed by a single, unified API with features like the built-in player ↗︎ and analytics ↗︎ that make it easy to get started.

How do I get started

First, create a live input ↗︎ using cf ↗︎, the API, or in the Stream Dashboard ↗︎:

The response will include webRTC and webRTCPlayback properties, each containing a url for WHIP (broadcast) and WHEP (playback) respectively.

Next, you can go live using WHIP directly from a browser or supported broadcast software. Refer to our new tutorial ↗︎ that shows a dependency-free way to broadcast live video with browser-native JavaScript.

Finally, you can play using WHEP using Stream’s built-in player ↗︎, a supported player app/library, or simple JavaScript:

Learn more in the Stream WebRTC docs or try the all-in-one tutorial for yourself.

Pipecat PhoneLLM Mini now available on Workers AI

Workers AIRealtime

@cf/daily-co/phonellm-mini-alpha-2, a model from the Pipecat ↗︎ team at Daily, is now available on Workers AI. PhoneLLM is built for voice agents and other realtime AI applications, where a model has to reply quickly and call the right tool mid-conversation.

In a voice agent, the language model sits between speech-to-text and text-to-speech, so every second it takes adds to the caller's wait. Developers usually choose between a fast model without reasoning mode, which can miss instructions or tool calls, and a slower model in reasoning mode, which handles both well. Pipecat post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano 30B on phone and customer support scenarios so PhoneLLM follows instructions and calls tools better without reasoning mode.

You can use PhoneLLM through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()) or the REST API at /ai/run. Pipecat recommends temperature: 0. Also set chat_template_kwargs: { enable_thinking: false }.

Run a voice agent with Pipecat on Workers

Pipecat ↗︎ is an open-source Python framework for building voice agents. Now that Python Workers are generally available, you can run a Pipecat voice agent on Cloudflare.

Our Pipecat voice agent example ↗︎ runs in a Durable Object and uses WebRTC as the voice transport through the Realtime SFU. It uses DeepSeek V4 Flash by default. To deploy it with PhoneLLM, give this prompt to your coding agent:

For more information, refer to the PhoneLLM Mini model page, Pipecat's model card ↗︎, and Workers AI pricing.

Oct 14, 2026

Infrastructure applications support a configurable session duration

Cloudflare OneAccess

Infrastructure applications now have a configurable session duration with a default value of 24 hours. You can set the session duration when creating or editing an infrastructure application in the dashboard or via the API.

When the session duration elapses, any active SSH connections through that application will be closed, and users will need to reconnect. Previously, infrastructure applications did not enforce a session duration limit. Sessions could persist beyond 24 hours in some cases, but were never guaranteed beyond 10 hours due to Gateway connection limits.

When a target matches multiple infrastructure applications, the shortest session duration applies.

For more information, refer to Session duration.

Oct 14, 2026

Configure Advanced Custom Nameservers with nameserver sets (beta)

DNS

Nameserver sets are now available in beta to Enterprise accounts. A nameserver set groups two to five custom nameserver names with Cloudflare-assigned IP addresses. You can assign the set to zones in the same account.

Enterprise customers using Cloudflare DNS can create Advanced Custom Nameserver sets. These sets distribute addresses across Advanced anycast network groups to improve resiliency.

Compared to legacy custom_ns sets, modern nameserver sets offer several advantages:

  • Sets are reusable objects. Accounts are no longer limited to 5 numbered sets. Create a set once and assign it to one or more zones in the same account.
  • Custom address counts. Assign each nameserver up to 3 IPv4 and 3 IPv6 addresses. This allows for more flexible setups.
  • Diverse addresses. IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are now both selected from a diverse set of prefixes for increased redundancy.
  • Support for Advanced Custom Nameservers. Set advanced to true to allocate addresses from Advanced anycast network groups, providing the same benefits as Cloudflare branded Advanced nameservers to your custom nameservers.
  • Explicit changes. Sets are immutable, so adding or removing a nameserver name never changes the configuration of zones that already use a set.

Create a set by sending a POST request to /accounts/{account_id}/dns_settings/nameserver_sets with the following body:

Then, send a PATCH request to /zones/{zone_id}/dns_settings with the returned nameserver set ID:

This configures the zone to use the nameserver set.

For more information, including other setup steps, refer to Nameserver sets.

Legacy custom_ns sets remain supported. A single account can use both.
